## Step 1: Create the integration

1. Open WSO2 Integrator.
2. Select **Skip for now**.
3. Select **Create New Integration**.
4. Set **Integration Name** to `ConnectAGitRepository`.
5. Set **Project Name** to `connect-git-repository`.
6. Select **Create Integration**.
7. Select **ConnectAGitRepository**.

## Step 2: Connect a Bitbucket repository

1. <!-- manual: Sign in to [WSO2 Cloud](https://console.devant.dev/). -->
2. In the console header, select **Organization** list and select your organization.
3. In the left navigation menu under **Admin**, select **Settings**. This opens the organization-level settings page.
4. Select **Credentials**.
5. Select **+ Add Git Credentials**.
6. Enter a **Credential Name** and select **Bitbucket** as the Git provider.
7. <!-- manual: Enter a Credential Name and select Bitbucket as the Git provider. -->
8. <!-- manual: Enter your Bitbucket Username. -->
9. <!-- manual: Enter the App Password obtained from Bitbucket. :::tip See the [Atlassian documentation](https://support.atlassian.com/bitbucket-cloud/docs/create-an-app-password/) for instructions on creating an app password in Bitbucket. ::: -->
10. Select **Save**.

## Step 3: Connect a GitLab repository

1. <!-- manual: Sign in to [WSO2 Cloud](https://console.devant.dev/). -->
2. In the console header, select **Organization** list and select your organization.
3. In the left navigation menu under **Admin**, select **Settings**. This opens the organization-level settings page.
4. Select **Credentials**.
5. Select **+ Add Git Credentials**.
6. Enter a **Credential Name** and select **GitLab** as the Git provider.
7. <!-- manual: Enter a Credential Name and select GitLab as the Git provider. -->
8. <!-- manual: Enter the Server URL of your GitLab self-managed instance. -->
9. <!-- manual: Enter the Access Token obtained from GitLab. :::tip See the [GitLab documentation](https://docs.gitlab.com/user/profile/personal_access_tokens/#create-a-personal-access-token) for instructions on creating a personal access token in GitLab. ::: -->
10. Select **Save**.

## Step 4: Connect an Azure DevOps repository

1. <!-- manual: Sign in to [WSO2 Cloud](https://console.devant.dev/). -->
2. In the console header, select **Organization** list and select your organization.
3. In the left navigation menu under **Admin**, select **Settings**. This opens the organization-level settings page.
4. Select **Credentials**.
5. Select **+ Add Git Credentials**.
6. Enter a **Credential Name** and select **Azure DevOps** as the Git provider.
7. <!-- manual: Enter a Credential Name and select Azure DevOps as the Git provider. -->
8. <!-- manual: Enter your Azure DevOps Organization Name. -->
9. <!-- manual: Enter the Access Token obtained from Azure DevOps. :::tip See the [Azure DevOps documentation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/devops/organizations/accounts/use-personal-access-tokens-to-authenticate?view=azure-devops&tabs=Windows) for instructions on creating a personal access token in Azure DevOps. ::: -->
10. Select **Save**.
